title: Mouse support: click tabs, rows and keys (M toggles capture, off at launch)

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Owners who use the pointer want to click tabs, rows and project keys. docs/dashboard.md:12 says mouse clicks do the same as keys. Decided: record 129 (ui.mouse): off in v1; if built, opt-in. Mouse capture also blocks terminal text selection, which matters for copying the slicer land command (docs/dashboard.md:102-103). Owner decision 2026-10-28 (interactive): the opt-in is a toggle key in the TUI, not a launch flag: `m` turns capture on and off at run time (off at every launch, not persisted), so selecting text is one key away. Bubble Tea v2.1: the mode is set on the View value (v.MouseMode), and clicks arrive as tea.MouseClickMsg.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
The toggle key is `M` (owner decision 2026-10-30; `m` is the Roadmap matrix pane since S168).

- `TestMouseOffByDefault`: View() leaves MouseMode off and a click message changes nothing (adj 129).
- `TestMouseKeyTogglesCapture`: `M` sets MouseMode to cell motion, `M` again clears it; the status line says `mouse on` while it is on; a new Model starts off.
- `TestMouseKeyIsInTheHintAndHelp`, plus goldens for the help overlay (`go test ./internal/tui -update`, review the diff in `testdata/golden/`).
- `TestClickViewTabSwitchesView`: a click on a view tab does what tab does.
- `TestClickSidebarProjectSelectsIt`: a click on a project row does what its digit key does.
- `TestClickOverviewRowMovesCursor`: a click on a drawn row moves the cursor to that row, allowing for the inline run pane (S106) and the scroll offset.
- `TestClickOutsideRowsDoesNothing`.
- `TestClickWhileConfirmBarOrHelpOpenChangesNothing`: ui.confirm (adj 98) stays in charge.
- `TestMouseKeyIgnoredInTextInput`: `M` typed into an answer or filter field stays text.

Each fails first because no mouse handling or `M` binding exists.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Tests first. Re-anchor from the code (view.go sets AltScreen; the key dispatch in model.go; the tab bar and sidebar renderers record their cell ranges). 1. Add `mouse bool` to Model (false at start), key `M` toggles it outside text input and the confirm bar; View() sets v.MouseMode = tea.MouseModeCellMotion when on. 2. Record hit rectangles while drawing: each view tab, each sidebar project row, each Overview/Running/Roadmap row (reuse the row-start bookkeeping from S151 and the selExtra scroll offset so a click lands on the drawn row, not the data row). 3. Handle tea.MouseClickMsg (left button) in Update: tab, sidebar row or list row, with the same effect as the key; ignore the wheel in this slice. Clicks do nothing while a confirm bar, help overlay or text field is open. 4. Status line shows `mouse on`; the hint bar offers `M mouse` low priority (dropLine high so it goes first); help overlay lists it (watch the 100x30 help headroom noted on S164). 5. docs/dashboard.md:12 and :102-103 name the toggle and the text-selection trade-off. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Acceptance criteria:

- At launch the TUI does not capture the mouse: terminal text selection works and a click changes nothing (adj 129).
- 'M' turns capture on and the status line shows 'mouse on'; 'M' again turns it off and the cue goes away. Capture is off again at the next launch.
- With capture on, a left click on a view tab, a sidebar project row or an Overview, Running or Roadmap row does exactly what the matching key does; the wheel does nothing.
- A click outside any row, or while the confirm bar, the help overlay or a text field is open, changes nothing; 'M' typed into a text field stays text.
- The hint bar offers 'M mouse' and the help overlay lists it; docs/dashboard.md names the toggle and the text-selection trade-off.

Commands:

- `go test -race ./internal/tui` exits 0 and lists the nine tests named in Failing tests as passing.
- `go vet ./...` exits 0.
- `go test ./...` exits 0.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check --root /home/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork` and `adj lint` exit 0.
- [HUMAN CHECK] At 100x30 and 80x24 in a real terminal: select text with the mouse at launch, press `M`, click a tab, a project and a row, press `M` again and select text again.
